To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed a 1  km product of SWC for the CONUS and tested the accuracy of the globally available datasets in the CONUS.
(1) the use of globally available datasets for estimating soil calibration parameters for CRNP measurements is feasible and (2) a vegetation index can be used to estimate the biomass water signal.
the use of global datasets of soil clay percent, soil bulk densities, and soil organic matter can be used to estimate soil lattice water with an RMSE of 0.035 g cm3 and a R2 of 0.68.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of globally available datasets to support the operatibility of roving CRNP for field-scale SWC mapping in the CONUS.
the development of a 1  km product of SWC using CRNP data and a globally available soil dataset.
the use of globally available datasets for estimating soil water content at the field scale using the roving CRN method.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the roving CRN method has been shown to be accurate and robust for field-scale soil water measurements, but the method still requires a local calibration to accurately estimate soil water content.

the global dataset is a viable option for supporting CRNP measurements in the CONUS, but it should be considered an initial estimate that should be refined by local soil and biomass calibration parameters when they are available.
the global soil calibration dataset developed in this work can be applied to estimate SWC with the roving CRPN method in CONUS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the roving CRNPs are capable of estimating field-scale SWC with an RMSE  =  ∼0.04 cm3  cm−3, but this is dependent on the accuracy of the soil parameters.
we developed a globally available soil calibration dataset for the CRNP, and we developed a methodology for estimating biomass water signal in the CRNP signal.

the global datasets of soil texture, soil bulk density and soil organic carbon can be used to estimate SWC with an RMSE of 0.05 cm3  cm−3, but the vegetation biomass water signal must be accounted to achieve the desired accuracy of SWC estimation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

globally available datasets can support the operability and accuracy of the roving cosmic ray neutron probe in large surveys and novel environments, and that these datasets are accurate enough to be used for SWC estimation in the continental United States.
global datasets can be used to estimate local calibration parameters for the CRNP, which may allow for the development of a roving CRNP method for estimating field SWC.
global soil datasets can be used to develop a 1 km product of soil calibration parameters that can improve the operability of roving CRNPs.
